recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not restore the obsolete verificationStatus example or old extension reference; future changes should be driven by the later Condition status/bodyStructure issues rather than by the original DSTU2 wording.
issue_request: FHIR-11281 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU2 Patient Care request to make Condition.verificationStatus optional with an unknown default, add verificationStatus comment text for cases such as abdominal pain in the ED, and add Condition.bodySite guidance that bodySite is used only when not implicit in Condition.code and that richer body-site attributes should use the then-current body-site-instance extension.
initial_application: Git commit f6747b5dae067e2b72852f858c8004070b307fcd applied the original request to the old Condition spreadsheet source by changing Condition.verificationStatus from 1..1 to 0..1, adding the ED example comment and unknown default, adding GF#11281 committee notes, and adding the requested Condition.bodySite comment with the extension reference.
additional_context: The current source is generated from structuredefinition-Condition.xml rather than the old spreadsheet. Later applied decisions explain the current wording: FHIR-16193 changed clinicalStatus and verificationStatus from code to CodeableConcept; FHIR-54914 replaced the verificationStatus comment and removed the unclear abdominal-pain example; FHIR-39630 added Condition.bodyStructure Reference(BodyStructure), added the bodySite/bodyStructure invariant, and removed the old body-site extension reference. FHIR-31027 is related bodySite/BodyStructure background that preceded the later base-resource element change.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Condition is active in source/fhir.ini; current Condition.verificationStatus still has GF#11281 committee notes and cardinality 0..1, and current Condition.bodySite still says it is only used if not implicit in Condition.code. Reintroducing the older ED example or body-site extension pointer would conflict with later applied Jira decisions.
